top_story: Houthi forces’ capture of a strategic island near the Bab al-Mandab on 12 September widened their leverage from Yemen’s battlefield to a core maritime chokepoint, sharpening pressure on Saudi exports and global shipping. That shift was followed on 14 September by drone and missile strikes into Saudi Arabia and a pipeline shutdown, which pushed oil above $109 and showed how quickly localized escalation can spill into energy markets and civilian economic strain across the region. In Israel, renewed scrutiny of Benjamin Netanyahu’s handling of pre-October 7 warnings deepens mistrust in political leadership at a moment when regional insecurity is again exposing failures of deterrence and crisis preparation. The emerging picture is of a Middle East where armed non-state actors are expanding coercive reach while governments face growing credibility costs at home and rising external economic fallout.
